citations.quote: By definition, then, that bond’s key-rate ’01 with respect to that key rate would equal its yield-based DV01 while its key-rate ’01 with respect to all other key rates would be zero.
Because the yield on the x-bond is 5% today, the level equation (6.25) predicts that the yield on the y-bond will be 5% today, despite its being 1% yesterday.
Solution to 2: Despite the significant differences in times-to-maturity (10, 20, and 30 years), the approximate modified durations on the three bonds are fairly similar (4.768, 5.169, and 5.063).
